content.text: {"concept_key":"c5-math-fractions-basics","title":"Understanding Fractions","quick":"A fraction shows a part of a whole, written as parts you have over total equal parts. Think of sharing one roti among friends.","full":"A fraction has two numbers: the bottom number (denominator) tells how many equal parts the whole thing is cut into, and the top number (numerator) tells how many of those parts we are talking about. Example: cut one roti into 4 equal pieces, give 1 piece to Ishika. She has 1/4 of the roti. If she gets 3 pieces, she has 3/4. The whole roti must be cut into EQUAL parts, otherwise it is not a proper fraction. Children often confuse fractions with whole numbers or think bigger denominator always means bigger piece, but 1/4 is smaller than 1/2 because the roti is cut into more pieces, so each piece is smaller.","traps":["Thinking a bigger denominator means a bigger piece","Forgetting the parts must be equal, not just any pieces","Mixing up numerator and denominator positions"],"misconception":"Child thinks 1/8 is bigger than 1/2 because 8 is a bigger number than 2.","parent_questions":[{"q":"If I cut a roti into 2 equal parts and give you 1 part, what fraction do you have?","expected_answer_hint":"1/2, because one part out of two equal parts"},{"q":"Which is bigger, 1/3 of a roti or 1/6 of a roti?","expected_answer_hint":"1/3 is bigger, because fewer, larger pieces when roti is cut into 3 parts"}],"check_question":{"q":"A chocolate bar is cut into 5 equal pieces. Ishika eats 2 pieces. What fraction did she eat?","options":["2/5","5/2","2/3"],"correct_index":0,"right_feedback":"Correct! 2 pieces out of 5 equal pieces is 2/5.","wrong_feedback":"Not quite.
